The test image shows a tomato fruit with circular, sunken lesions featuring dark gray/black centers with concentric rings and visible fungal sporulation (acervuli). This is the classic macroscopic presentation of Anthracnose on tomato fruit caused by *Colletotrichum* spp.

The reference image (Bugwood_4) shows the microscopic conidia of the Anthracnose pathogen, confirming the disease category. The Bugwood IDs on both images (5475189 and 5475194) are from the same source collection.

Key diagnostic features in the test image:
- Circular, sunken lesions on ripe tomato fruit
- Dark black/gray fungal sporulation masses (acervuli) in lesion centers
- Concentric ring pattern around lesions
- Multiple coalescing lesion sites
